plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single three-dimensional sketch of a vector broken into components. Three axes meet at a common origin, x pointing toward the lower left and out of the page, y running to the right, and z pointing straight up, each drawn as a thin line with an arrowhead and an italic label. A dashed rectangular box is built on the origin with its edges lying along the three axes. Three heavy blue arrows run outward along those axes and are labeled as the component vectors: A_x = A_x i-hat along the x-axis, A_y = A_y j-hat along the y-axis, and A_z = A_z k-hat along the z-axis, with each label written alongside its arrow. A single red arrow starts at the origin, cuts diagonally through the interior of the box, and ends at the far corner where the dashed faces meet; it is labeled A = A_x + A_y + A_z, every symbol carrying an overhead vector arrow. Drawing the blue arrows as three edges of the box and the red arrow as its body diagonal lets the reader watch the three components add head to tail to rebuild the whole vector. The same box supports the two nested right triangles from which the magnitude of a three-dimensional vector is obtained.

elements: common origin point where the x, y, and z axes meet
thin black x-axis arrow starting at the origin and pointing diagonally down-left, slightly out of the page
thin black y-axis arrow starting at the origin and pointing horizontally to the right
thin black z-axis arrow starting at the origin and pointing vertically upward
italic axis labels x, y, and z placed at the arrow tips
dashed rectangular component box with one corner at the origin and the opposite corner at the resultant vector tip
dashed edges parallel to the x-axis, y-axis, and z-axis outlining all visible sides of the box
dashed top-face and side-face guide edges showing how the far corner is reached from the three components
heavy blue component arrow A_x along the positive x direction from the origin
heavy blue component arrow A_y along the positive y direction from the origin
heavy blue component arrow A_z along the positive z direction from the origin
label for the x component: vector A_x = A_x i-hat, rotated along the diagonal x arrow
label for the y component: vector A_y = A_y j-hat, placed above the horizontal y arrow
label for the z component: vector A_z = A_z k-hat, rotated vertically beside the z arrow
heavy red resultant arrow vector A from the origin to the far upper-right corner of the dashed box
label for the resultant: vector A = vector A_x + vector A_y + vector A_z, placed along the red diagonal arrow
small arrowheads on all blue component vectors and on the red resultant vector
live magnitude annotation |A| = sqrt(A_x^2 + A_y^2 + A_z^2), placed unobtrusively near the figure

interactions.label: Preset vector case
interactions.teaches: The learner distinguishes an axis-aligned vector, a planar vector, and a genuinely three-dimensional vector by seeing which components are nonzero.

interactions.label: A_x
interactions.teaches: Changing A_x changes only the extent of the box and component arrow in the x direction, while the resultant adjusts to the new far corner.

interactions.label: A_y
interactions.teaches: Changing A_y shows how the horizontal component contributes independently to the resultant vector's length and direction.

interactions.label: A_z
interactions.teaches: Changing A_z makes the resultant rise or flatten, revealing the vertical part of a three-dimensional vector.

interactions.label: Construction mode
interactions.teaches: The learner sees that the three blue component vectors can either be drawn from the origin as projections or placed head to tail to produce the same red resultant.

demo_steps.title: Axis-aligned vector
demo_steps.narration: Only A_x is nonzero, so the red resultant lies exactly on the x-axis and overlaps the blue A_x component. The dashed box collapses to a single diagonal edge.

demo_steps.title: Vector in the xy-plane
demo_steps.narration: With A_z set to zero, the resultant stays flat in the xy-plane. The box becomes a rectangle, and the red vector is the diagonal of that base.

demo_steps.title: Full three-dimensional vector
demo_steps.narration: Now all three components are nonzero. The red vector reaches the far upper corner of the dashed box, showing A as the body diagonal determined by A_x, A_y, and A_z.

demo_steps.title: Head-to-tail addition
demo_steps.narration: Switching construction mode moves the blue arrows into a chain: A_x first, then A_y from its head, then A_z from that head. The final tip is unchanged, confirming that the component sum equals the red resultant.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use an oblique textbook-vector projection matching the source: mathematical +y is screen-right, mathematical +z is screen-up, and mathematical +x is the receding diagonal drawn down-left at about 45 degrees. The default component box dimensions are A_x × A_y × A_z = 1.5 × 3.5 × 3.0 source-axis units, where A_x is along the down-left receding axis, A_y is horizontal right, and A_z is vertical up. The common origin sits slightly left of center and below mid-height. Draw thin black axes extending beyond the blue component arrows: x to about 2.2 units down-left from the origin, y to about 4.2 units right, z to about 3.5 units up. Draw the dashed box from O = (0,0,0) to the far corner (A_x,A_y,A_z), with all dashed edges in black or dark gray, dash length about 0.12 units. In simultaneous mode, the blue arrows all start at the origin: A_x from O to (A_x,0,0), A_y from O to (0,A_y,0), and A_z from O to (0,0,A_z). In head-to-tail mode, draw A_x from O to (A_x,0,0), then A_y from (A_x,0,0) to (A_x,A_y,0), then A_z from (A_x,A_y,0) to (A_x,A_y,A_z). The red resultant always runs from O to (A_x,A_y,A_z). Colors: blue component arrows #173f70 or #123a68, red resultant #c74444, black axes and labels #111111, dashed box #333333. Component arrows should be thick cylinders or tubes with conical arrowheads; red resultant should be similarly thick and slightly more visually prominent. Labels should be black italic math text, with vector arrows over A symbols and hats over i, j, k. Magnitude formula: |A| = sqrt(A_x^2 + A_y^2 + A_z^2), updated numerically from slider values.
interactionPlan.notes: Keep the default view close to the source figure: no perspective convergence, z vertical, y horizontal, x down-left. Implement the oblique projection as a fixed camera/projection transform or by placing mathematical axes into screen-oriented world directions. Preset selection should update the three sliders to representative values: x-only sets A_y=A_z=0, xy-plane sets A_z=0, and full xyz restores all three nonzero. Sliders remain editable after choosing a preset. When constructionMode is Head-to-tail build, animate the translated blue arrows sequentially over about 1 second each, then leave them in the head-to-tail positions; when switching back, return the three blue arrows to the origin-edge layout. Hide labels for zero-length component arrows or fade them to avoid overlap at the origin.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Preset vector cases: choose x-only, xy-plane, or full xyz components and the component arrows plus resultant update, showing when a vector is axis-aligned, planar, or genuinely spatial.
- Slider for component values A_x, A_y, and A_z: learner adjusts each component with separate controls; the box dimensions, blue edge arrows, and red resultant update together; the relationship between components and resultant magnitude or direction becomes visible.
- Toggle between simultaneous components and head-to-tail build: learner switches the construction mode; the blue arrows either sit on the box edges or animate sequentially from one arrowhead to the next before ending at the red vector tip; the equivalence between component decomposition and vector addition becomes clear.

authoredContext:
In three-dimensional space, vector A→ has three vector components: the x-component A→x=Axi^, which is the part of vector A→ along the x-axis; the y-component A→y=Ayj^, which is the part of A→ along the y-axis; and the z-component A→z=Azk^, which is the part of the vector along the z-axis. A vector in three-dimensional space is the vector sum of its three vector components (the figure):

This expression for the vector magnitude comes from applying the Pythagorean theorem twice. As seen in the figure, the diagonal in the xy-plane has length Ax2+Ay2 and its square adds to the square Az2 to give A2. Note that when the z-component is zero, the vector lies entirely in the xy-plane and its description is reduced to two dimensions.

A vector in three-dimensional space is the vector sum of its three vector components.

Vector A in the x y z coordinate system extends from the origin. Vector A equals the sum of vectors A sub x, A sub y and A sub z. Vector A sub x is the x component along the x axis and has length A sub x I hat. Vector A sub y is the y component along the y axis and has length A sub y j hat. Vector A sub z is the z component along the z axis and has length A sub x k hat. The components form the sides of a rectangular box with sides length A sub x, A sub y, and A sub z.

discrepancies: The A_x component arrow is much shorter and partly obscured near the origin compared with the clearly visible down-left blue component in the source.
An extra magnitude formula label is added above the box, which is not present in the source figure.
The A_x label is crowded around the origin and less readable/faithfully placed than in the source.
The dashed cuboid is close but has lighter gray, more open dashed styling than the darker dashed construction lines in the source.
evaluation.notes: The generated figure is very recognizable and conceptually correct, with strong 3D vector-component geometry and useful controls, but the x-component and its label are less faithful and an extra magnitude annotation is introduced.
action_items: Increase or reposition the visible A_x component so it more closely matches the prominent down-left blue arrow in the source.
Move the A_x label away from the origin and align it more cleanly along the x-component arrow.
Remove or make optional the magnitude formula label if the goal is strict visual fidelity to the source.
Darken the dashed construction box lines slightly to better match the original textbook styling.
